subject: Maths
title: Volume of prisms and cylinders
subtitle: Volume and Surface Area · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can calculate the volume of prisms and cylinders using the formula V = area of cross-section times length.

key_vocab.definition: The volume of a prism equals the area of its cross-section multiplied by its length. A cylinder is a circular prism, so its volume = πr²h.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can calculate the volume of prisms and cylinders using the formula V = area of cross-section times length.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: volume -- The volume of a prism equals the area of its cross-section multiplied by its length. A cylinder is a circular prism, so its volume = πr²h.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Volume of any prism = area of cross-section multiplied by the length (or height) of the prism.
V = A × l
A = area of the uniform cross-section, l = length of the prism

Key examples:
  ✓ Cuboid: V = l × w × h  (rectangle cross-section × length)
  ✓ Cylinder: V = πr²h  (circle area × height)
  ✓ Triangular prism: V = ½ × b × h × l  (triangle area × length)
  ✗ Volume = surface area × height  (volume uses cross-section area, not surface area)
  ✗ Cylinder V = 2πrh  (that is the curved surface area, not volume)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – cuboid
  Find the volume of a cuboid 8 cm by 5 cm by 3 cm.
  Cross-section area = 8 × 5 = 40 cm²
  Volume = 40 × 3
  = 120 cm³
  120 cm³
  (A cuboid is a rectangular prism.)

Example 2 – cylinder
  Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 4 cm and height 10 cm. Round to 1 d.p.
  Cross-section area = πr² = π × 4² = 16π
  Volume = 16π × 10 = 160π
  = 502.7 cm³
  502.7 cm³
  (Substitute into V = πr²h.)

sections.title: Cuboids
sections.content:
Find the volume of each cuboid.

(a) 6 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm
(b) 10 cm × 5 cm × 2 cm
(c) 8 cm × 8 cm × 8 cm
(d) 12 cm × 3 cm × 5 cm

sections.title: Cylinders
sections.content:
Find the volume of each cylinder. Round to 1 d.p.

(a) r = 3 cm, h = 10 cm
(b) r = 5 cm, h = 8 cm
(c) r = 2 cm, h = 15 cm
(d) r = 7 cm, h = 6 cm

sections.title: Triangular prisms
sections.content:
Find the volume of each triangular prism.

(a) Base 8, height 5, length 12 cm
(b) Base 10, height 6, length 9 cm
(c) Base 7, height 4, length 20 cm
(d) Base 12, height 3, length 8 cm

sections.title: Other prisms
sections.content:
Find the volume using V = A × l.

(a) Trapezium: parallel sides 4, 8; height 3; length 10 cm
(b) Cross-section area 25 cm², length 14 cm
(c) L-shape cross-section area 32 cm², length 6 cm
(d) Hexagonal cross-section area 42 cm², length 9 cm

sections.title: Mixed volume problems
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) Cylinder: diameter 10 cm, height 7 cm. Volume?
(b) Prism volume = 360 cm³. Cross-section area = 30 cm². Find length.
(c) Cylinder volume = 200π cm³. Height = 8 cm. Find the radius.
(d) Cuboid: l = 9, w = 4. Volume = 252 cm³. Find h.
(e) Triangular prism: base 6, length 10. Volume = 180 cm³. Find height of triangle.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Volume of a prism = area of cross-section × length
✗ Volume of a cylinder = 2πrh
✓ V = πr²h requires the radius, not the diameter
✗ Volume and surface area use the same formula
✓ Volume is measured in cubic units such as cm³
